Welcome to Newnham St Peter's Church of England Primary School
Welcome from the headteacher,Mr. Child
It is with great joy and pride that I welcome you to Newnham St Peter's C of E Primary School. Whether you are a prospective parent, a current member of our community, or simply curious about who we are, I hope this website gives you a clear sense of our vision, values and the vibrant life of our school.
We believe every child is a unique gift from God and our school is a place where kindness, respect and curiosity are nurtured and flourish. We strive to create a safe and inspiring environment where children feel loved, challenged and empowered to become the best version of themselves.
From forest school adventures to collective worship, we aim to ignite a lifelong love of learning. We are proud of our dedicated staff, our supportive families and our strong links with the local parish, which help make our school a true community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Newnham St Peter's Church of England Primary School - Our Vision
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Newnham St Peter's Church of England Primary School
Our Vision
Our Vision
Cherish Everyone, Flourish Together, Serve Others
At Newnham St Peter’s Church of England Primary School, our vision, "cherish everyone, flourish together, and serve others," is deeply rooted in the essence of love, faith, and hope. Inspired by the boundless love of our faith, we cherish every child, nurturing their unique gifts and building a community where all can flourish. Together, we learn, grow, and explore, our roots grounded in faith and our branches reaching for the stars. Through service to others, we share the fruits of our blessings, reflecting the divine light in every act of kindness.
Rooted in the teachings of Jesus, love is woven into the fabric of our school's identity, influencing every aspect of our mission to ignite a passion for learning and personal growth, empowering students to embrace challenges, pursue excellence, and realise their dreams with unwavering determination.
The timeless Christian value of love serves as the compass that directs our decisions, shapes our curriculum and our pastoral care practices, and inspires our community engagement efforts.
We are committed to cultivating an inclusive and compassionate educational environment where love is the cornerstone, nurturing the growth, character, and success of every individual.
Rooted in the teachings of Jesus, love is the cornerstone of our school's identity. Love influences every aspect of our mission, igniting a passion for learning and personal growth. We are committed to creating a nurturing atmosphere where every child, adult, and staff member feels valued and supported. By promoting open dialogue, valuing differing perspectives, and fostering an atmosphere of acceptance, we create an inclusive community where each member is cherished. We prioritise the spiritual, emotional, and intellectual well-being of each individual, encouraging curiosity, exploration, and self-discovery. This environment allows children to explore their faith journey, ask questions, and deepen their understanding of Christian values.
Our school community thrives when we work in harmony, just as a garden flourishes when tended to collectively. We believe in the power of unity, collaboration, and mutual support. Hope empowers our students with a sense of optimism and resilience. Through a dynamic curriculum, innovative teaching methods, and a commitment to continuous improvement, we equip our pupils with the skills and confidence to navigate an ever-changing world. By encouraging teamwork, celebrating shared achievements, and providing opportunities for collaborative learning, we enable every individual to reach their full potential.
Guided by Christian faith, we recognise the importance of selfless service to others and the necessity of enabling our children to be global citizens aware of their impact on the earth. Faith inspires our children to channel their talents, skills, and compassion toward making a positive impact on society and caring for the planet. Through acts of service and community engagement, we put our love into action, extending a helping hand to those in need and making a positive impact in the world. Our pupils are empowered to carry the value of love beyond our walls, becoming compassionate leaders and ambassadors of goodwill.

Collective Worship
Inclusive, Invitational, and Inspirational Worship
At Newnham St Peter's, collective worship is a cornerstone of our school community. Our approach to worship is designed to be inclusive, invitational, and inspirational, ensuring that every member of our school community feels welcome and valued.
Understanding Spirituality
We explore spirituality through the concepts of "Wows," "Ows," and "Nows":
Working with the Church and Clergy
Our relationship with the local church and clergy is vital to our collective worship. We work closely with the church to integrate the colours and themes of the liturgical calendar into our worship practices. This partnership enriches our worship, providing depth and context to our spiritual journey throughout the year. Clergy members regularly visit our school to lead worship, share insights, and support our community's spiritual growth.
Worship Structure: Gather, Engage, Respond, Send
Our collective worship follows a structured yet flexible format that enhances the spiritual experience:

pageCache.pageTitle: Newnham St Peter's Church of England Primary School - St Peter's Church
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Newnham St Peter's Church of England Primary School
St Peter's Church
St Peter's Church
Our school is a Church of England school and has close links with St Peter’s Church in Newnham.
Our Christian foundation shapes the life of our school. We seek to be an inclusive community of faith, hope and love, with a particular focus on love. This underpins our vision: ‘cherish everyone, flourish together and serve others’. In practice, this means everyone is welcome to be part of our school community, where we seek to grow in understanding of all people, those of any faith and none.
Staff and children visit St Peter’s Church for school services every month, to which families are also invited. We use the church as a resource to support the RE curriculum and members of the church community are involved in the everyday life of the school.
In school, collective worship takes various forms during the week. Staff and children help to lead worship for the whole school and in their classrooms. They have opportunities to ask ‘big questions’ about life and faith, to which all answers are welcomed and explored. Each classroom has a prayer corner; children are encouraged to engage with prayer in a way which is accessible and relevant. Children are given the tools to become global citizens, aware of the needs of others and of the earth.
As a Church School we have a Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS) Inspection every five years. At our last inspection in 2017, our school was judged to be outstanding. In 2023, a new inspection framework was introduced. It explores how a school’s theologically rooted Christian vision shapes its work and enables the school to live up to its foundation as a Church School.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Newnham St Peter's Church of England Primary School
PE and Sport Premium
PE and Sport Premium
The 'PE and Sport Premium' funding is a government initiative designed to ensure that all young people have the opportunity to lead healthy and active lives. Recognising the importance of a positive experience in sports and physical activities, the funding aims to establish a lifelong habit of participation, aligning with the government's vision for a world-class education system.
Engaging in physical activity not only contributes to the physical health of children and young people but also enhances their mental well-being. It has been linked to increased self-esteem, emotional well-being, and a decrease in anxiety and depression. Physically active children tend to be happier, more resilient, and display greater trust in their peers. Moreover, providing pupils with sufficient daily activity can have broader benefits for both individuals and schools, positively impacting behaviour and academic achievement.
In line with the School Sport and Activity Action Plan, the government is committed to ensuring that children and young people have access to a minimum of 60 minutes of sport and physical activity daily, with a recommended 30 minutes delivered during the school day. This aligns with the Chief Medical Officers' guidelines advocating for an average of at least 60 minutes per day throughout the week.
The PE and Sport Premium empowers primary schools to work towards this objective by making additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of PE, physical activity, and sports programs. Directly allocated to schools, this funding offers flexibility, allowing them to tailor its use to best suit the needs of their pupils.
The government believes in granting headteachers and school leaders the autonomy to decide how to utilise the funding for PE and Sports in their schools. Accountability for these decisions is maintained through:

Religious Education
At Newnham St Peter’s Church of England Primary School, our Religious Education (RE) curriculum follows the Gloucester Diocesan Scheme of Work and incorporates the Understanding Christianity framework. pageCache.pageTitle: Newnham St Peter's Church of England Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Newnham St Peter's Church of England Primary School
Music
Music
The Power of Music in Education
Music is more than just a form of entertainment; it is a vital part of education that enriches students’ lives in numerous ways. From enhancing cognitive abilities to fostering emotional growth, music education plays a crucial role in the holistic development of children. Studies have shown that students who engage in musical activities often perform better academically, demonstrating improved reading and maths skills. The rhythmic and melodic patterns in music help to develop the brain’s ability to process complex patterns, which translates into better problem-solving skills and higher academic achievement.
Emotional and Social Benefits
Engaging with music allows children to express their emotions and develop empathy. Whether through singing, playing an instrument, or simply listening, music provides a safe outlet for emotions and helps children understand and connect with their feelings. Additionally, participating in group musical activities, such as choir or band, fosters teamwork and social skills. These experiences teach children the value of collaboration and communication—essential skills that will benefit them throughout their lives.
Creativity and Motor Skills
Music education encourages creativity and imagination. When children create their own music or interpret existing pieces, they learn to think outside the box and explore new ideas. This creative process enhances their ability to innovate and solve problems in unique ways. Furthermore, playing musical instruments helps develop fine motor skills and hand-eye coordination. The precise movements required to play an instrument improve dexterity and coordination, which are beneficial in many other areas of life.
National Curriculum Overview
The National Curriculum recognises that music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. A high-quality music education should engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, thereby increasing their self-confidence, creativity, and sense of achievement. As pupils progress, they should develop a critical engagement with music, allowing them to compose and listen with discrimination to the best in the musical canon.
The national curriculum for music aims to ensure that all pupils:
Perform, listen to, review, and evaluate music across a range of historical periods, genres, styles, and traditions, including the works of great composers and musicians.
Learn to sing and use their voices, create and compose music on their own and with others, have the opportunity to learn a musical instrument, use technology appropriately, and progress to the next level of musical excellence.
Understand and explore how music is created, produced, and communicated, including through the interrelated dimensions: pitch, duration, dynamics, tempo, timbre, texture, structure, and appropriate musical notations.
At Newnham St. Peter's, we use Kapow, a fantastic online music curriculum that provides a structured sequence of learning, offering a range of creative resources alongside teaching specific tuned instrumental units. We are looking to enrich this further by collaborating with Gloucestershire Music School's peripatetic teachers to give our children experiences with different instruments to practice the skills they have learned in the curriculum (Gloucestershire Music).
Please read our Curriculum Intent, Implementation, and Impact document as part of our Music Curriculum, which outlines what we teach, why we teach it, and when.
Our choir has the opportunity to participate in Young Voices, which provides wonderful enrichment and a chance to be part of a larger musical performance. This event allows our pupils to perform alongside thousands of other young singers, creating a memorable experience that fosters a sense of community and belonging.
In addition to Young Voices, our choir performs at various events in our local community, including seasonal concerts, church services, and community festivals. These performances not only showcase the talents of our pupils but also strengthen our ties with the community, allowing us to share the joy of music with others.
This year, music is a significant focus in our School Improvement Plan, and we aim to harness a love of music across the school while offering more musical opportunities for all pupils. We believe that by investing in music education, we are enriching our pupils' lives and helping them develop essential skills that will serve them well in the future.

Welcome to Newnham St Peter's Church of England Primary School
Remote Learning
Remote Learning
At Newnham St Peter’s, we are committed to ensuring that all children continue to learn, grow, and flourish, even when they are learning from home. Whether your child is learning remotely due to illness, isolation, or wider school closure, we aim to provide a consistent and supportive learning experience.
Our Remote Learning Offer
We use Seesaw as our main platform for remote learning. Through Seesaw, pupils can:
Access daily lessons and resources in line with the class curriculum
Upload completed work for feedback from teachers
Watch recorded or live teaching sessions (where applicable)
Stay connected with their teacher and peers
We also provide a weekly timetable and clear expectations for each day to help structure learning at home.
What You Can Expect
For children working from home, we provide:
A broad and balanced curriculum that mirrors in-school learning as closely as possible
Daily English and maths lessons, plus phonics or reading for younger pupils
A range of foundation subject tasks (e.g. Science, History, RE, art)
Regular feedback to encourage and support progress
Opportunities for prayer, reflection, and maintaining connection with our Christian vision
Support for Pupils and Families
We understand that home learning can be challenging for families. We aim to make remote learning:
Accessible – Tasks are adapted to suit different needs and age groups
Flexible – We understand families have different routines and devices
Supportive – Staff are available via Seesaw to answer questions and offer encouragement
If you need printed materials, extra support, or a loan of a device, please contact the school office. We are here to help.
Online Safety Reminder
When learning online, it’s important to keep children safe. Please visit our Online Safety page for tips and resources to help you support safe and sensible screen time at home.
Helpful Remote Learning Links
Seesaw Login – Access daily learning activities
Oxford Owl – Free eBooks and reading support
White Rose Maths – Video tutorials and worksheets
BBC Bitesize – Learning resources across the curriculum
Top Marks – Interactive games for all subjects

Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND)
Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND)
At Newnham St Peter's we value the contribution that every child makes and we welcome the diversity of culture and learning styles. The school seeks to raise achievement, remove the barriers to learning and increase physical and curricular access for all. All children and young people with Special Educational Needs (SEN) are valued and respected as equal members of the school. Provision for pupils with SEN is a matter for the school as a whole. All teachers are teachers of pupils with SEN.
A child or young person has special educational needs if he or she has a learning difficulty or disability which calls for special educational provision to be made for him or her. The four broad areas of need which we provide for are:
At Newnham St Peter's we follow the graduated pathway to support pupils with SEND. Parents and carers will be involved at every stage. We offer all pupils quality first teaching by working at the pupil's stage, using appropriate materials and supporting where required within class.
Our Special Needs Co-ordinator is Mrs Samantha Howells. She may be contacted through the School Office.
Address: Newnham St Peter Church of England Primary School, Station Road, Newnham, Gloucestershire, GL14 1AT
Telephone: 01594 516208
Email: admin@nspschool.uk
As part of the 'Children's and Families Act 2014' every provider for additional needs is required to give a summary of what it can offer to help support and care for pupils that may require additional support in school. This is known as the 'SEND Information Report'.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Newnham St Peter's Church of England Primary School
Clubs
Breakfast Club will open from 7:45 am. The cost to book is £5.00 per session and breakfast is included.
Places are limited to 18 places per day and are allocated on a first come, first served basis.
After School Club is available to book as follows...
If your child attends a sports club, there is an option for your child to join the after-school club at the end of their sports club session. Please book your child’s sports club place as normal and book your required after-school session separately.
A range of activities will be offered, including crafts, board games and indoor play, planned around the children’s interests, topical and calendar events.
A light snack is included for children who are in attendance at the time of serving (approx 4:15pm).
Places are limited to 18 places each day and are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.
Available to book via SchoolMoney app.
Each hobby club is limited to 25 places allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, each term. Sessions run from 3:15–4:15pm at £5 per session.
Booking and Payment Terms
Wraparound (Breakfast and After-school) and Sports/Hobby club places are bookable and payable in advance of sessions via our school payment system, Eduspot/SchoolMoney. At the end of each half-term, the booking system will be available for the upcoming term - a text will be sent to notify parents/carers when clubs are available to book via the website eduspot.co.uk or app ''Teachers2Parents'.
Acceptance of your payment via eduspot is confirmation that your child has a place at the club/s you have requested. Please check if you have received a receipt before sending your child to a club.
Bookings should be received by the published deadline date for hobby clubs (see termly posters). Breakfast and after-school club are taken offline every Thursday for the upcoming week.
Session requests received after the booking has been taken offline will be charged at a higher rate due to the additional administrative time required, unless it is a genuine emergency.
An additional £2.00 will be added to each session. The revised session charges are as follows.
Childcare Voucher Scheme and Tax-Free Childcare
We are registered to accept childcare vouchers and Tax-Free Childcare as payment for clubs. If you would like to pay this way, please email Jo Young at earlybirds@nspschool.uk for further details.
Breakfast and After-school Club
If you wish to book a place for your child/children, you will be required to select sessions by day, for each week in the term. The booking system allows for irregular patterns of attendance to accommodate parents who work irregular shifts. We aim to be as flexible as possible with both our breakfast and after-school clubs and offer the option to pay weekly / fortnightly / monthly or termly in advance to suit your needs. However, we impose a strict deadline for booking the Thursday prior to the week you require wraparound. Once the booking has been taken offline, there will not be an option to book a place for your child/children, unless for an exceptional circumstance such as a one-off emergency. In this instance, please contact the office or email earlybirds@nspschool.uk to check availability.
To cancel your child's place, we require a 24-hour notice by emailing earlybirds@nspschool.uk and a credit will be applied to your account. A charge will apply if we do not receive a 24-hour notice.
Sports & Hobby Clubs
If you wish to book a place for your child/children, you will be required to select and pay for your chosen activity for the full term. If part way through the term your child decides they no longer wish to attend the club, please email earlybirds@nspschool.uk, and we will issue a credit for the remaining sessions. No credits are offered for ad hoc sessions missed.
If you experience any issues with booking, have any questions, or require a password reset, please contact Jo Young - earlybirds@nspschool.uk.
If you are unable to pay online, unique reference barcodes are available from the school office. Payments can then be made at any paypoint store. Our nearest paypoint stores are Elton Garage or Littledean Stores. Please register your interest by emailing Jo Young and, once paid, send your receipt to the school office detailing the club/s you have registered for.
If your child is entitled to Free School Meals (not universal Infant Free School Meals), please apply for a free place either via email, communication book or phone.

pageCache.pageTitle: Newnham St Peter's Church of England Primary School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Newnham St Peter's Church of England Primary School
Curriculum
Cherish everyone, flourish together, and serve others.
Rooted in the eternal values of faith, hope and love (1 Corinthians 13:13), we believe every child is created in the image of God, with unique gifts and the potential to grow. Our curriculum is designed to nurture every child spiritually, academically, emotionally and socially, preparing them to live life in all its fullness (John 10:10).
At Newnham St Peter’s, we believe that every child deserves access to meaningful, challenging learning. That’s why our curriculum follows a “low threshold, high ceiling” approach—creating a learning environment that is both inclusive and ambitious.
This directly reflects our vision:
Every child can access the learning and feel valued from the start, regardless of their starting point.
Low Threshold – Inclusive by Design We start from the belief that every child is loved by God and deserves full access to rich, meaningful learning. Tasks are designed to be clear, welcoming and accessible to all learners, including those with SEND, EAL, or other additional needs.
We achieve this through:
This reflects the faith we hold in each child’s God-given worth and potential. To cherish everyone means not just allowing participation, but actively designing learning so that everyone belongs and everyone can succeed.
Children are encouraged to think deeply, ask big questions, and develop their full God-given potential in the community.
High Ceiling – Challenge for All While all children access the core learning, our curriculum builds in opportunities for depth, creativity, and extended thinking. Children are supported to:
This is where we see children truly flourishing together—not racing ahead, but growing in wisdom, confidence, and collaboration. It reflects our commitment to hope: that every child can go further than they ever imagined, supported by a loving and inspiring community.
Learning is never just for ourselves. Through collaborative learning and open-ended tasks, children are encouraged to use their knowledge and skills in ways that serve and bless others.
Learning That Leads to Love in Action Because our curriculum is rooted in purpose and Christian values, pupils are empowered to:
This is love in action, as taught in 1 Corinthians 13: “the greatest of these is love.” We want our children not only to know more, but to be more—faith-filled, thoughtful, and compassionate individuals who live out their learning for the good of others.
Examples in Practice
What Difference It Makes
Every child at Newnham St Peter’s is:
“Low threshold, high ceiling” is not just a teaching strategy. At Newnham, it is a Christian expression of faith, hope and love in action.
Our Curriculum Helps Children Grow:
The Newnham Difference
Every child is seen, known, and celebrated at Newnham St Peter’s. They leave us ready not only for the next stage of education, but for a life of meaning, contribution, and joy—ready to live life in all its fullness, aspiring, believing, and achieving together.
